newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FOCUS-Virgin eyes UK short-haul market.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Virgin eyes UK short-haul market.

text.p: JOHANNESBURG, Oct 3, Reuter - Entrepreneur Richard Branson looked forward to breaking into the busy British domestic airline market on Thursday as he launched his latest Virgin Atlantic long haul service, from London to Johannesburg.

Speaking of his separate Virgin Express airline, based in Brussels, he told Reuters: "Virgin Express is where the really rapid expansion is taking place at the moment and we may be able to say a bit more about that in the next few days."

"In Europe it is now possible to create a real pan-European airline which can really take the major airlines apart and it has been great fun so far doing that, reducing fares and still making a profit," he said.
"It has been very satisfying but the problem is we have not been able to connect Britain yet...and that is something that we may have more to say about soon," he said.

Five months ago Virgin said the British shorthaul market was already highly competitive compared with the rest of Europe and its main target for expansion would be overpriced mainland routes dominated by national carriers.

But Branson said he had now decided he also wants to move in on his home market while continuing to expand in mainland Europe, having whetted his appetite for controversy with the launch of contentious new cut-price services from Brussels to Copenhagen and Rome to Madrid last month.

Virgin Express was created in April with Branson's takeover of European regional carrier EuroBelgian Airlines SA for 38 million pounds ($60 million). Its declared aim was undercutting major operators on European short-haul routes which become open to totally free competition in April next year with the advent of the EU's single aviation market.

Meanwhile he said his long-haul carrier Virgin Atlantic Airways also plans to press ahead with the expansion of its network next year. His plans include the launch of new routes from London to Antigua, Barbados and St Lucia in the Caribbean and to Shanghai, Singapore and Bangkok.
He said Virgin would also like to fly direct services from London to Cape Town.
During the inaugural flight to Johannesburg, Branson told Reuters the service would open the way for the rest of his retailing and entertainment empire to move into South Africa.

He said plans were in hand to open up Virgin Megastores selling books, games and records in the country. He also intended to serve the airwaves with a new radio station and supply the nation's palate with Virgin Cola and Virgin Vodka.

Funding for Virgin Atlantic's expansion will come from cashflow, he said. New services this year and next will help boost sales at his Virgin travel group division which embraces the airlines as well as his holidays business to around 900 million pounds in the year to end-August 1997, from an expected turnover of 650 million pounds in the year just ended.
"Financially the airline is very strong and we are making a lot of cash which we are using to expand," he said.

But the proposed alliance between arch rivals British Airways and American Airlines has put a freeze on his expansion plans for transatlantic services. These would have added Chicago, Philadelphia and other major U.S. cities to Virgin's existing destinations of New York, Washington, Boston, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Orlando and Miami.

Virgin has been campaigning furiously to get the proposed alliance blocked, arguing that it would dominate the British transatlantic market with control of over 60 percent of all flights. Britain's Department of Trade and Industry is about to decide whether or not to refer the alliance to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission for a lengthy investigation.
"As far as new Americn routes are concerned we have got everything on hold at the moment until we know where we stand on that (the BA/American alliance)," he said. ($1=.6388 Pound)
